notes.meaning: God's people gather at Zion, His dwelling place, ready to offer Him worship. True praise sometimes begins in quiet wonder before it bursts into song, because God's goodness is too great for words. Worshippers also come to fulfill the promises and gifts they pledged when they cried out for His help.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some commentators doubt that David wrote this psalm. They point out that it speaks of the Temple and its courts, which were built after his time.

notes.meaning: God welcomes everyone who calls on Him and delights to answer their requests. Because He hears and cares, people of every kind and from all nations are invited to approach Him in prayer.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Ellicott accepts that the verse points to the gospel spreading to all nations. But he thinks the psalmist himself meant something narrower: every nation may pray to God, while praise in Zion was Israel's special privilege.

notes.meaning: Even when sins feel too heavy to carry and defeat us, God provides the forgiveness we need. To atone means to cover over or wipe away our guilt so we are made right with God. He graciously removes the burden of our wrongdoing through His mercy.
It is a great joy to be invited into God's presence and to live in close fellowship with Him. Those who come to worship in His house find deep spiritual satisfaction in His holy goodness and peace.

differ.view: God freely chooses certain people. By His special grace He draws them near and makes them able to come.
Believers are chosen for Christ's sake and accepted in Him, not because of anything in themselves.
The chosen ones here are the priests picked to serve at God's house. Ordinary worshippers still share in its blessings.
The one chosen is Israel as a people, brought back into the blessings of God's covenant (His binding promise).

notes.meaning: God answers the prayers of His people with wonderful, awe-inspiring acts that deliver them and set things right. Because His saving power reaches everywhere, He is the true hope of people across the entire earth, even on the farthest seas.

God established the giant mountains firmly in their places by His own mighty strength. The picture is like a strong builder strapping on a belt for work, showing that the stability of the physical world rests entirely on Him.
The Lord has the power to calm wild, crashing ocean waves with a single word. In the very same way, He is able to silence angry mobs and quiet the turmoil of warring nations.

People living in the most distant parts of the world stand in awe when they see the wonders of God's power in nature. From the rising of the sun in the east to its setting in the west, each day brings reasons to shout for joy.
God personally cares for the ground by sending showers to make it fruitful and rich. His heavenly supply of water never runs dry, making sure crops can grow to feed humanity.
Rain poured from the sky fills the plowed furrows and softens the hard soil. These gentle showers prepare the ground so new seeds can sprout, grow, and flourish under God's blessing.
A plentiful harvest is like a glorious crown placed at the end of the farming year by God's kindness. Wherever God moves through creation, His footsteps leave behind rich, overflowing abundance.

Even dry, unplowed wilderness lands receive enough rain to produce green pasture for grazing herds. The hills look as though they have put on festive robes because they are completely wrapped in fresh life and joy.

Pastures are so filled with grazing sheep that they look dressed in white wool, while the valleys are blanketed with golden grain. All of nature joins together in a triumphant song of praise to the God who provides for all living things.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Keil and Delitzsch argue that fields cannot sing. They think the ones shouting and singing are the people, who rejoice over the harvest.
